cohort: 120 healthy pregnant women aged 20-40, seeking epidural analgesia during active labor (cervix 3-4 cm dilated) with uterine contractions and uncomplicated term labor (37-41 weeks gestational age).
finding: The Combined Spinal-Epidural (CSE) group demonstrated a faster onset of analgesia and lower pain scores at 15 minutes compared to the epidural group, but also experienced a longer second stage of labor and a higher need for extra dosage, with no significant differences in most maternal or fetal outcomes, or mode of delivery.
mod_finding: The mode of delivery was similar between the two groups, with normal vaginal delivery rates of 88.33% in the CSE group and 83.33% in the epidural group.
followup_time: Intrapartum (throughout labor stages) and immediate post-birth (Apgar scores)
